complexity.notes: The pop-then-expand trick avoids the usual 'only start from run beginnings' check and is elegant, though slightly less conventional than the canonical sequence-start approach; readability is still good.
complexity.summary: Builds a set of the values, then repeatedly pops an arbitrary element and expands outward to consume its entire consecutive run, tracking the maximum run length. Each element is removed from the set exactly once, giving linear total work on average.
